newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Cotton prices in India, Pakistan seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Cotton prices in India, Pakistan seen falling.

text.p: Cotton prices in India and Pakistan are likely to fall in the next few days on increased arrivals from farms, dealers said on Thursday.
In India, cotton prices firmed on a new export quota announcement but fell back later on increased arrivals in the domestic markets, dealers said.
"Release of the additional export quota for cotton by the government helped an early price rise, but later on the rally petered out on higher new crop supplies," one trader said.

The Indian government released an extra 345,000 (170-kg) bales of cotton for export in the 1996/97. Earlier it had allowed export of 150,000 bales. In 1995/96 the government authorised exports of 1.65 million bales.
In spot deals, Bengal-deshi (ready delivery) rose up to 900/925 rupees from 870/890 rupees but then fell to 880/900 rupees per maund.
Crop prospects had improved after recent rains in Punjab killed whitefly that had been damaging the plants.
"I think the crop will be over 10 million bales," one source said. Pakistan produced 9.95 million bales in 1995/96 (July-June).
The government has promised to maintain a free export/import regime for cotton at least until June 1998.
